title: Finite-coefficient compact-support projection formula
statement:
Fix the finite-field datum [def-weil-finite-field-fiber]
and finite coefficient ring $A=A_{E,n}$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension].
Let $f:X\to Y$ be a
separated finite-type
morphism of finite-type $k$-schemes [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], [def-weil-proper-morphism].
On the small etale sites, let
$K\in D^b_c(X_{\mathrm{et}},A)$ and
$L\in D^b_c(Y_{\mathrm{et}},A)$, in the
derived categories of
bounded complexes with constructible cohomology [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories], [def-weil-pbc-constructible-complexes].
Assume $L$ has
finite Tor amplitude,
using the tensor-vanishing definition on the etale site [def-kun-tor-amplitude].
The projection transformation,
formed with the
ordinary etale derived tensor [def-kun-derived-tensor] and exact pullback [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact]
and the compact-support
direct image [def-amb-etale-compact-support], is an isomorphism:

$$
Rf_!K\otimes_A^L L
\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ } Rf_!(K\otimes_A^L Lf^*L).
$$

It is natural in $K,L$.
The same assertion holds for their pro-etale realizations equipped
with etale-origin witnesses [def-weil-pbc-etale-origin-witness],
where the representatives satisfy the displayed hypotheses.

The etale transformation is the compactification composite of the proper counit-defined map [def-kun-projection-formula-map] and the canonical open tensor comparison, with the compact-support identifications of [lem-amb-etale-compact-comparisons]. The pro-etale transformation is the finite constant-coefficient composite of [def-exchange-projection]; realizations use [def-sf-comparison-derived-pullback].

proof.text: Work first with ordinary constant-$A$ modules on the small etale sites. The coefficient ring is finite and commutative by [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. A field is Noetherian (its only ideals are zero and the unit ideal). The locally-finite-type assertion in [pqf-def-locnoeth], applied to the structure maps, makes $X,Y$ locally Noetherian. Their finite-type structure maps are quasi-compact by [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], so a finite subcover of an affine Noetherian cover makes them Noetherian. Choose an arbitrary compactification $c=(j,p)$ by [sk-thm-nagata-sketch-noetherian]. Its proper $p$ is of finite type and quasi-compact by [def-weil-proper-morphism] and [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]; the same argument over a finite Noetherian affine cover of $Y$ makes $\overline X$ Noetherian. Its open $j$ is quasi-compact: $\overline X$ is quasi-separated by [lem-weil-pbc-locally-noetherian-quasi-separated], and $X$ and each affine open $V\subset\overline X$ are quasi-compact opens, so their intersection is quasi-compact by [pqf-lem-qs-intersection-qc]. This intersection is the inverse image $j^{-1}V$. On $D^+$ the coherent comparisons [lem-amb-etale-compact-comparisons] allow us to compute $Rf_!$ as the candidate $Rp_*j_!$ of [def-amb-etale-compact-support]. Define the etale compact projection map using this computation as $Rp_*(\gamma)\circ\pi_{p;j_!K,L}$, where $\pi$ is precisely the counit-tensor-identity mate of [def-kun-projection-formula-map] and $\gamma:j_!K\otimes^Lp^{-1}L\to j_!(K\otimes^Lf^{-1}L)$ is the open tensor comparison constructed in step 3. We prove invertibility for every choice $c$; thus computing the compact-support transformation using any chosen compactification, or transporting its source and target along the coherent functor comparisons, gives the asserted invertibility. No equality of transformations for different compactifications is being assumed from mere independence of the functors.

source.place: paragraph 1: choose a compactification and form the projection composite; Stacks 01T6, 0B56

proof.text: Check all bounded-below domains before base change. Choose integers $u\leq v$ outside which the cohomology of $K$ vanishes, and a representative $C$. First form $C_{\leq v}$ by replacing $C^v$ by $\ker(d_C^v)$ and deleting degrees $>v$; its inclusion into $C$ is a quasi-isomorphism. Then form $E$ by quotienting its degree $u$ by the incoming boundaries and deleting degrees $<u$. The quotient map $C_{\leq v}\to E$ is a quasi-isomorphism, since it leaves cohomology in degrees $\geq u$ unchanged and the deleted cohomology vanishes. Thus $C\leftarrow C_{\leq v}\to E$ is an explicit quasi-isomorphism zigzag and $E$ is supported in $[u,v]$. When $u=v$, the sole term is $E^u=\ker(d_C^u)/\operatorname{im}(d_C^{u-1})$; the zero object may be represented by the zero complex. By the explicitly etale clause of [lem-sf-flat-model], choose a bounded flat representative $H$ of $L$, supported in some $[a,b]$. The hypothesis $\ell\ne p$ makes $\ell$ invertible on these $k$-schemes, as required there. By [lem-kun-kflat-criteria](1), $H$ is K-flat. Constant-coefficient inverse image is exact by [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact]; moreover [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback] says pullback of this K-flat flat-term model is again K-flat with flat terms. Thus $K\otimes^Lf^{-1}L$ is represented by the total tensor $E\otimes f^{-1}H$, supported in $[u+a,v+b]$. There are only finitely many summands in each total degree. Extension by zero is exact by [lem-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero-exact], so $j_!E$ is still bounded. The module-coefficient derived direct image of [def-weil-pbc-direct-image] carries $D^+$ to $D^+$; hence $Rf_!K$, $Rf_!(K\otimes^Lf^{-1}L)$, and also $Rf_!K\otimes^LL$ are bounded below. For the last assertion tensor a bounded-below representative of $Rf_!K$ with the same bounded flat $H$. No Tor-amplitude assumption on $K$ is used.

source.place: paragraph beginning Both base-change applications are legitimate; Stacks 07A4, 0G7E

proof.text: Here is the open comparison, including its normalization. For etale module sheaves $F$ on $X$ and $B$ on $\overline X$, use [lem-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero-adjunction] to form $\kappa:j_!(F\otimes j^{-1}B)\to(j_!F)\otimes B$, the transpose of the unit $F\to j^{-1}j_!F$ tensored with $j^{-1}B$. On germs inside $X$ it sends $s\otimes t$ to $s\otimes t$; outside $X$ both sides are zero by [lem-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero-stalks] and the ordinary stalk-tensor isomorphism [lem-pod-etale-stalk-tensor-scalar](1). Thus [lemma-weil-pbc-geometric-stalk-conservative] shows $\kappa$ is an isomorphism of sheaves (the inverse of a bijective linear map is linear). Apply this in each bidegree to $E$ and $p^{-1}H$. All maps are natural, hence commute with both differentials and their total-complex signs. Exactness of $j_!$ [lem-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero-exact] and the K-flat pullback assertion of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback] identify this total-complex isomorphism with the corresponding derived one. Its inverse is $\gamma$. This proves the required etale open projection isomorphism, rather than importing the pro-etale-only version. The construction also works on every base-changed compactification, with the pulled-back bounded flat model.

source.place: 03S5 (extension by zero stalks and exactness); blueprint proof paragraphs 1-2, with the inverse adjunction map written out

proof.text:
Fix any geometric point $g:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to Y$; write $f_g:X_g\to\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$ and $c_g=(j_g,p_g)$ for the base-changed morphism and compactification. Set $E_g=g'^{-1}K$ and $P=g^{-1}L$. The stalk-as-pullback identification [lem-kun-stalk-as-pullback] and the first assertion of [lem-kun-0ezp] let us regard $P$ as an object of $D(A)$: an etale object over $\Omega$ is a disjoint union of points, so the sheaf axiom determines a module sheaf by its value on that point, with products on disjoint unions. This equivalence and its inverse preserve the tensor unit, tensor products and complexes. By [lem-kun-inverse-image-monoidal] and [thm-cbc-finite-torsion], applied to both $K$ and $K\otimes^Lf^{-1}L$ (step 2), the source and target of the pulled-back compact projection map identify respectively with
$$R\Gamma_c(X_g,E_g)\otimes_A^LP,\qquad R\Gamma_c(X_g,E_g\otimes_A^L\underline P),$$
where $\underline P=f_g^{-1}P$. The base-change theorem permits arbitrary $g$: neither finite type of $g$ nor constructibility on the fiber is an extra hypothesis. The source complexes lie in $D^+$, $A$ is finite, $j$ is quasi-compact and $p$ is proper, exactly as that theorem requires.

source.place: paragraph beginning Let a geometric point; Stacks 07A4 and 0EZP

proof.text:
The identifications in step 4 carry the actual map to the compact projection map for $f_g$, not just its objects. Indeed [def-cbc-exchange-map] factors the compact exchange as the proper mate followed by the open base-change comparison. For the proper square, [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-exchange-tensor-coherence], with $E=j_!K$ and $Q=L$, asserts exactly the equality between exchanging after projection and projecting after exchange, with the specified tensor comparisons. For the open square, the comparison of [lem-cbc-extension-zero-base-change] is the inverse of the mate of the open-adjunction unit. Its compatibility with $\kappa$ from step 3 can be checked by transposing to $j_g^{-1}$: both composites are the pulled-back unit tensored with the pulled-back second factor; on a local elementary tensor $s\otimes t$ each sends it to the pair of pulled-back sections. Bilinearity gives equality on tensors, sheafification gives equality of sheaf maps, and naturality gives equality in every total-complex degree. The derived open base-change is precisely this termwise map by [cor-cbc-derived-extension-zero-base-change]. Inverting the two $\kappa$ maps gives the equality for $\gamma$. Combining the proper equality and this open equality proves that the stalk map is exactly
$$\alpha_P:R\Gamma_c(X_g,E_g)\otimes_A^LP\longrightarrow R\Gamma_c(X_g,E_g\otimes_A^L\underline P).$$

source.place: 0E48 (exchange/projection square); blueprint actual-map paragraph, with the open unit-mate calculation expanded

proof.text: By the explicitly etale assertion of [fix-lem-finite-tor-perfect], $P=L_{\bar y}$ is represented by a bounded finite-free complex $F^\bullet$ over $A$. It suffices to prove the proper projection map for $p_g$ with fixed first input $j_{g!}E_g$ and variable second input $P$ on $\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$. The open projection is already an isomorphism by step 3. By [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-projection-mate-exact], both proper-map functors are exact, the transformation is natural and commutes with shifts and the connecting arrows of triangles, and at $P=A$ it is the identity. Naturality with the inclusions and projections of finite direct sums therefore identifies its component at $A^r$ with the direct sum of $r$ identity components. Shift compatibility gives the assertion for $A^r[-i]$. To build $F^\bullet$, remove its lowest nonzero degree $i$: the subcomplex of degrees $>i$ and the quotient $F^i[-i]$ form a degreewise split short exact sequence. The associated triangle is distinguished by [lem-weil-pbc-degreewise-split-derived-triangle]. Induct on the number of nonzero terms, starting with the zero complex and the one-term case; [lem-sf-triangle-morphism-iso] applied to the morphism of triangles makes the remaining vertical map an isomorphism. Naturality transports this conclusion across the quasi-isomorphism $F^\bullet\simeq P$. Thus the proper component and hence $\alpha_P$ are isomorphisms. This uses the pointwise finite-free representative, not a claim that $L$ is locally perfect as a sheaf complex. Retracts, although also stable under naturality and splitting, are not needed because the stalk model is finite free.

source.place: 0944 (perfect projection formula devissage); blueprint bounded finite-free stalk argument, written out for the proper factor

proof.text: Steps 4-6 show that every geometric pullback of the etale compact projection map is an isomorphism. Apply [lem-kun-stalk-faithful-derived] to its underlying abelian-sheaf complex map: forgetting $A$-module structure preserves the kernels, images and cokernels that compute cohomology, and a vanishing underlying cohomology sheaf is a vanishing module sheaf. Hence its cone is acyclic as a module complex and the etale map is an isomorphism. Its naturality in $K,L$ follows from the natural counit and tensor maps of [def-kun-projection-formula-map] and the natural open-adjunction construction in step 3. This proves the etale assertion for the arbitrary compactification selected in step 1.

source.place: last sentences of the etale argument: conservativity and naturality

proof.text:
For the pro-etale assertion put $C_T=\nu_T^*$. This is the exact termwise derived comparison of [lem-sf-comparison-pullback-exact] and [def-sf-comparison-derived-pullback]. The ring identification in the former and [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback] give its canonical derived tensor comparison. Pullback comparison is [lem-weil-pbc-comparison-pullback]. Let $c_j:C_{\overline X}j_!^{et}\simeq j_!^{pro}C_X$ be [lem-cbc-proetale-extension-zero-comparison], extended termwise; exactness on the pro-etale localized site is [lem-pur-site-restriction-module-adjunction-exact], using the open-site identification of [lem-weil-proetale-weakly-etale-localization]. For proper $p$, quasi-compactness follows from its finite-type definition and quasi-separatedness from [lem-pc-separated-quasi-separated]. Thus [lem-weil-pbc-comparison-direct-image-canonical-mate] supplies the named isomorphism $b_p:C_YRp_*^{et}\simeq Rp_*^{pro}C_{\overline X}$, with its stated counit normalization, for every bounded-below input. Compose it with $Rp_*^{pro}(c_j)$ to obtain
$$B_H:C_YRf_!^{et}H\xrightarrow{\sim}Rf_!^{pro}C_XH.$$
This is the compact-support comparison on etale-origin inputs; its invertibility and naturality are also stated in [lem-sf-class-compact-support-comparison]. We need it for $H=K$ and $H=K\otimes^Lf^{-1}L$, which are bounded below by step 2. Exactness of $C$ keeps their realizations bounded below. All rings here are ordinary constant finite rings, with no completed or rational tensor products.

source.place: final paragraph: construct the compact-support comparison on the specified representatives; Stacks 09AF

proof.text:
Check compatibility with projection before transporting invertibility. For the proper factor use [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-exchange-tensor-coherence] on the commutative ringed-topos square formed by $p_{et},p_{pro},
u_{\overline X},
u_Y$. That lemma explicitly does not require a cartesian square. Its exchange map is exactly $b_p$ of [lem-weil-pbc-comparison-direct-image-canonical-mate], since both are adjunct to $C_{\overline X}(\varepsilon^{et})$ after the inverse of the specified pullback comparison; its equality therefore compares the actual counit-defined proper projection maps. For the open factor one can check the canonical $c_j$ of [lem-cbc-proetale-extension-zero-comparison] on adjunctions, rather than invoking pro-etale stalk conservativity. By [def-weil-pbc-site-comparison-morphism], $
u_*$ is restriction on etale test objects. Hence $j_{et}^{-1}
u_{\overline X,*}=
u_{X,*}j_{pro}^{-1}$: both evaluate a sheaf on the very same etale test scheme with the same restrictions and scalar actions. The extension adjunctions [lem-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero-adjunction], [lem-weil-extension-by-zero-adjunction], and the comparison adjunction in that definition give natural bijections
$$\operatorname{Hom}(C_{\overline X}j_!^{et}F,M)\simeq\operatorname{Hom}(F,j_{et}^{-1}
u_*M)=\operatorname{Hom}(F,
u_*j_{pro}^{-1}M)\simeq\operatorname{Hom}(j_!^{pro}C_XF,M).$$
The canonical $c_j$ is the isomorphism represented by these bijections (construct its two arrows by the images of the two identity maps; naturality makes their composites identities). In particular it identifies the open units. Transpose the proposed compatibility of $C(\kappa)$ and $\kappa^{pro}$ under $j_!^{pro}\dashv j_{pro}^{-1}$; after the pullback and tensor comparisons both transposes are that same unit tensored with the identity. The Hom bijection is injective, so the maps agree. This calculation is on sheaves and is natural in both arguments; apply it to the bounded flat model from step 2. The comparison pullback carries this model to a K-flat flat-term model by [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback]; the exact derived comparisons therefore give the same equality for derived tensors. Inverting $\kappa$ identifies the transported $\gamma$ with the canonical pro-etale open projection isomorphism [lem-cbc-extension-zero-projection-formula]. Combining proper and open equalities identifies $C_Y(\mathrm{PF}^{et})$ with precisely the pro-etale composite specified in [def-exchange-projection], under $B_K,B_{K\otimes^Lf^{-1}L}$ and the tensor/pullback comparisons. Thus $\mathrm{PF}^{pro}$ for $(C_XK,C_YL)$ is an isomorphism by step 7. Finally for arbitrary realizations with the witnesses of [def-weil-pbc-etale-origin-witness], conjugate this equality by the supplied two witness isomorphisms. Naturality of the same projection construction gives the stated map on those realizations and its naturality in $K,L$.
